parallel.requirements: The parallel run recognized the clean-room requirement, the need to clone pier 0.1.6 behavior, and the ban on source lookup or binary analysis.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent did brief initial probing, assigned eight explorer children to behavior areas, then assigned all implementation, build, compile.sh, and verification work to one coder child.
parallel.implementation: No implementation was completed. The run produced a large behavioral spec and fixtures, but agent-8 only read/probed before cancellation.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The final artifact remained effectively the original workspace with README, LICENSE, .git, and executable; no source tree or compile script was delivered.
parallel.verification: The parent captured fixtures for later differential testing, but no integrated clone build or acceptance test occurred before closure.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Core coding, final assembly, build verification, and evaluator-aligned testing were unfinished; official evaluation compile_failed with no tests run.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same reverse-engineering requirements and documented many pier behaviors through normal CLI execution.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One agent retained all responsibility for probing, implementation, build, verification, and delivery; no subagents or parallel delegation were used.
serial.implementation: The agent discovered cargo and rustc, observed no crates.io access, and stated it would use the Rust standard library, but continued probing and did not create a project.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The final artifact also contained only the original workspace files and no new compileable replacement codebase or compile script.
serial.verification: The run generated many behavioral observations but never built or tested a reimplementation against the oracle or official evaluator before timeout.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Implementation, final assembly, and verification were unfinished; official evaluation compile_failed with no tests run.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Recognized the benchmark as a clean-room CLI clone requiring behavioral probing of pier.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Recognized the same clean-room CLI clone task and began by reading docs and help output.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-recognition difference; both understood the task, though neither delivered code.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Split behavior discovery across eight explorer children and later assigned implementation to one coder child.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Kept all probing, implementation planning, and delivery responsibility in the main serial agent.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel separated exploration and implementation across agents; serial used one continuous owner.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Explorer findings were aggregated, copied to /tmp as a spec, and provided to the coder with fixtures.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Task knowledge stayed in one agent context and did not cross an inter-agent boundary.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced a large handoff boundary; serial did not have a cross-agent context interface.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parent did not implement; after the spec handoff, agent-8 read resources and did only ambiguity probes before cancellation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial probed deeply, found cargo and rustc, discovered external crates were unavailable, and planned standard-library Rust but did not implement.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a delegated but canceled implementation path; serial had a never-started local implementation path.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The implementation child was active when the parent turn was canceled and returned a failed stopped-before-finish result.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There was no child result lifecycle; the serial main active turn itself was canceled.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel lost a delegated implementation result; serial had no delegated result to join or retrieve.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel shared generated spec and fixture files through /tmp but did not create or merge implementation files in the final workspace.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used scratch configs under /tmp and did not create or merge implementation files in the final workspace.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Neither run had a concrete merge collision or final integration; parallel had handoff artifacts, while serial had only local scratch state.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel captured byte-exact fixtures but never built or ran an integrated clone before official compile failure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran many oracle probes but never built or verified a reimplementation before official compile failure.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both lacked end-to-end verification of a submitted clone; parallel's fixture capture was preparation, not acceptance.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel timed out after heavy tool, token, and subagent use, including a late canceled coder child.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also timed out, with no subagents and a single long probing trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both exhausted the cell budget, but parallel spent it across a completed exploration swarm plus a canceled implementation child.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluations are not discordant: both runs failed with compile_failed and 0 of 779 tests passed. The important process difference is that the parallel run used an eight-child investigation phase and a later implementation child that was canceled, while the serial run kept probing locally until its own active turn was canceled. Neither produced a compileable replacement codebase.
parallel_contributors: Investigation was completed as a separate parallel phase before implementation started.
The delegated implementation child was stopped before finalizing or returning a codebase.
serial_contributors: The serial agent performed a long single-agent behavioral probe and never created a source project before cancellation.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial discovered that external crates could not be fetched and planned a standard-library implementation, but no code was written.
Parallel produced a more consolidated specification handoff, but still had no completed implementation.
evaluator_effects: Both official evaluations stopped at compile_failed, so no behavioral testcases were run.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained labels identify realized parallel adverse patterns, not a discordant root cause

candidates.reason: The parent explicitly assigned the core implementation and compile.sh deliverables to agent-8; the owner was canceled, not absent.
No multiple component implementations were produced and left unreconciled, so there was no concrete integration ownership gap.
The coder prompt assigned Cargo project creation and compile.sh placement; final assembly failed because the child was stopped, not because assembly was unowned.
The parent planned a probe, implement, build, test, and deliver pipeline through the coder handoff; the pipeline did not finish after cancellation.
The gate was not one mandatory serial preflight or harness step; it was a broad multi-child investigation phase.
The parallel parent completed a separate explorer-swarm phase before assigning productive implementation, leaving coding to a late phase that did not produce a deliverable.
candidates.realized_consequence: Implementation was deferred until after the completed exploration swarm, so no active implementation existed during the large research phase and no deliverable was produced.
candidates.near_match_reason: The explorer fan-out returned successfully and was consumed; the directly evidenced boundary is sequencing investigation before implementation.

candidates.reason: The late implementation path is already captured by Serial Investigation and Early Child Termination, with no separate allocation episode.
Although fan-out was broad, all eight explorer children completed and the parent consumed their result; budget pressure came from the research-first phase.
Agent-8 had a broad implementation brief, but it was explicitly canceled before proving scope-driven inability to complete; cancellation is the direct lifecycle event.
The implementation child received the task, constraints, resources, deliverables, and acceptance expectations; no known requirement was omitted from the brief.
The run did not delegate separately owned implementation components expected to interoperate, so no missing cross-agent interface contract materialized.
The parent copied the full 1149-line swarm result and created fixtures; the coder read the spec rather than missing known transferred facts.
The handoff was large, but the coder read it and began probes; the unfinished outcome is better explained by late start and explicit cancellation.
No receiver consumed a handoff describing a superseded workspace, requirement, dependency, or decision state.
No incompatible child reports or contracts were left unadjudicated at an integration decision point.
The parent never presented the whole task as complete; the evaluator failure alone cannot establish unsupported completion.
There was no replacement or retry child repeating prior work without inherited checkpoints.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: The parent delegated the required implementation to agent-8, then the active turn was canceled and agent-8 returned failed before finishing.
candidates.realized_consequence: The implementation child stopped before producing or returning source code, so the final artifact lacked a compileable reimplementation.
candidates.near_match_reason: There was no later, separate parent decision to ignore a failed child; the direct event was the explicit cancellation of the active child.

candidates.reason: No complete candidate implementation or compatible component set existed for final promotion before closure.
No implementation change was merged after integrated verification; no integrated verification of a clone occurred.
The delegated implementation was not completed or retrievable, so there was no completed child result for the parent to join.
No verifier child produced a concrete finding that was trapped below the parent; explorer results were returned and consumed.
The child failure was simultaneous with parent cancellation; there is no independent later failure-handling or takeover decision beyond Early Child Termination.
The completed explorer swarm result was inspected and used to create a spec; agent-8 had no completed implementation result to ignore.
The parent did not simply wait blindly; it read the swarm result, saved a spec, captured fixtures, and launched the coder before cancellation.
No concurrent agents produced different implementation files or competing build paths requiring reconciliation.
No two live agents edited the same source or configuration file in the final workspace.
No non-entry source file produced or owned by another agent was replaced or deleted.
No agent replaced the required executable or submitted entry point during concurrent ownership; the original executable remained in the artifact.
No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replaced multiple final workspace outputs.
Shared workspaces were used for probing artifacts, but no unstable implementation provenance or write conflict materialized.
The /tmp spec and fixtures were deliberate handoff artifacts, not unintended contamination of probing, verification, or the reference environment.

retained_patterns.reason: The parallel parent used completed explorer children as a separate first phase and only afterward assigned productive implementation.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: Productive implementation started only after the completed exploration swarm and did not reach a delivered codebase.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: The fan-out itself returned and was used; the actionable boundary is deferring implementation behind the investigation phase.

retained_patterns.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing
retained_patterns.reason: The required implementation was assigned to an active child that was explicitly stopped before finishing.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: The active implementation child returned failed before producing or handing back source code for the final artifact.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: No separate failure-reassignment opportunity appears after the stop; the direct lifecycle error is early cancellation.

No Failure Takeover, Missing Implementation Join, Late Finalization, Oversized Child Task, and Blind Timeout Wait were rejected for the coder chain because Early Child Termination names the direct observed stop.
